entries.title: 17 Best Buy Black Friday Deals on Hot Tech (2026): Up to 65% Off
entries.summary: Score deals on WIRED-tested headphones, laptops, and soundbars.
entries.content:
Thanksgiving may be over, but Best Buy’s hottest tech deals for Black Friday are just beginning. That means there's still plenty of time to buy noise-canceling headphones for the trip home. And if you spent yesterday pulling espresso shots for a kitchen full of relatives, consider now your chance to upgrade your setup before the visitors come back in December.

I've sorted through Best Buy's Black Friday sale for deals on WIRED reviewers’ favorite gear we've tested and can vouch for, including our favorite wireless headphones and a longtime favorite espresso machine. I also found a deal on the Oura Ring I bought at Best Buy last year—for $100 less than I paid then.

For more great discounts, check out our Absolute Best Black Friday Deals.

Updated November 28, 2026: We've added new deals on Nintendo Switch 2, Apple AirPods Pro 3, and LG Micro RGB Evo, and ensured up-to-date prices.

Nintendo Switch 2 and Mario Kart World for $500

According to WIRED contributing reviewer Matt Kamen, Nintendo’s Switch 2 sports a bigger, sharper screen, sturdier magnetic Joy-Cons, and the ability to play nearly all your old Switch games. If it's on the wish list of someone you know, this bundle includes the console itself, the Mario Kart World download, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online.

AirPods Pro 3 for $150

We gave these earbuds a 9/10 when we reviewed them last year, and still consider them the best earbuds you can buy if you have an iPhone. This is the lowest price our team has ever seen them go, so you won't see them at this price for long. For more options, check out our Best Black Friday AirPods Deals.

A Fancy New Phone

Samsung's interesting, brand-new Galaxy Z Fold8 (8/10, WIRED Recommends) unfurls into a 7.6-inch display for wide-view typing and multitasking. WIRED reviewer Julian Chokkattu prefers this model to the pricier Fold8 Ultra ($1,700, on sale), praising the Galaxy's easier-to-open hinge and declaring it nicer to use in every way.

A Cutting Edge RGB TV

LG's Micro RGB Evo (8/10, WIRED Recommends) is our favorite RGB TV right now, and this discount is so steep I honestly did a double take. It stands out for its stunning color quality, with vivid, contrast-y colors and exceptional detail. 60 percent off this cutting edge 2026 television is a very good deal.

Trendy Headphones

Though the bass-forward Beats Studio Pro (7/10, WIRED Recommends) come in a range of fun colors, including navy, brown, and gray, the plain black ones are $150 off right now. They offer easy pairing with both Apple and Android devices, as well as head-tracking for spatial audio.

A Windows Laptop We Recommend

WIRED reviewer Luke Larsen likes this well-equipped laptop with its Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite chip and generously sized, 120-Hz refresh rate display. The battery life is excellent, and while it's not quite as sharp as a MacBook, it's a great value and upgrade over similarly equipped Windows laptops.

A Truly Excellent TV Deal

If you're looking for a TV under $1,000, the TCL QM6K QLED (8/10, WIRED Recommends) is your best bet, at a hefty $500 off. Former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata calls it “a versatile display that does just about everything well, from naturalistic colors to rich black levels and impressive clarity.” It's even got a 144-Hz refresh rate if you plan to use it for gaming.

Our Favorite Headphones

These are the best wireless headphones we've ever tested, featuring some of the best noise canceling you can buy, paired with 30 hours of battery power. They're the latest in the lineup, with a new, smaller case and memory-foam—augmented folding ear cups that make them easy to pack for travel.

Great Earbuds for Traveling

These earbuds weigh just 5.5 grams per bud—25 percent smaller and 20 percent lighter than the previous model. Our reviewer loved them for their detailed and balanced sound, though he did find the noise canceling and call quality to be underwhelming. If you prioritize musical detail over bass, however, this sale makes them an excellent option to grab for your holiday travels.

A Crowd-Pleasing Espresso Machine

This Breville is the best semiautomatic espresso machine for most people, and reviewer Julian Chokkattu has been using the longtime WIRED favorite for seven years. We love its consistent pressure, steam wand, and built-in grinder, as well as the all-metal construction that's easy to clean.

The Smartest Android Phone

The new Google Pixel 11 is only a minor upgrade over last year's Pixel 10, which is still a solid phone with its 5X telephoto lens, magnetic Qi2 wireless charging, and impressive seven years of software support from launch. Note that this early deal is on unlocked 128-GB models in Indigo (shown) and Frost.

A Pretty OLED Gaming Monitor

Samsung makes some of the best gaming monitors, and this model is one of our top picks. Get all the gaming out of your system before the holidays on this 360-Hz refresh-rate screen that displays deep blacks and rich, accurate colors. These qualities also make this an excellent pick for graphic design and video editing. Its high price was one of our reviewer’s main complaints, so if you've been in the market, consider this your lucky day.

Track Your Holiday Stress

Given the Oura Ring 5 release this year, it's no surprise that the previous Oura Ring 4 is seeing some deep holiday discounts. While our reviewer loves the 5’s slimmer, more lightweight design, I actually prefer the chunky look of the 4, which I bought at Best Buy last year (for $100 more than this sale price) and is still going strong. Note that the $249 deal is only on the matte black and silver colorways.

Keep Your Holiday Guests Connected

Google’s Nest Wifi Pro 6E router (7/10, WIRED Recommends) is easy to set up and manage through the Google Home app, and WIRED reviewer Simon Hill found its coverage to be reliable during simultaneous gaming, streaming, and video calls. (Note that this deal is on one unit only, despite the two shown in the picture.)

A Gaming Mouse

With Stream Deck integration and a longer battery life than its predecessor, our reviewer says this is a good gaming mouse to consider. It's not the lowest price we've seen, but it's pretty solid if you're planning to buy one pre-holiday.

A Soundbar for the Subtitles-On Crowd

Are you always turning up the TV to hear what someone said? Especially if accents are involved? Could never be me, of course (spoiler: It's me), but if it is you, former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata loved this sleek, compact soundbar that sports AI Dialogue mode. It's a cool feature on an already high-quality soundbar that sharpens voices to make them easier to hear over music and action noises.

A Fitbit We Like

Our favorite Fitbit for beginners, the Charge 6 monitors your heart rate, blood oxygen, and skin temperature. It also offers features typically exclusive to more expensive trackers, including ECG and electrodermal activity scans. It's also got decent battery life for a Fitbit, at about a week.

entries.title: Best Black Friday Toy Deals (2026): Up to 50% Off Lego, Board Games, and Toys
entries.summary: Bag some gifts for your kids or unleash your inner child with the best Black Friday toy deals on Lego, STEM toys, and board games.
entries.content:
With the weather worsening, taking advantage of Black Friday toy deals and picking up discounted board games or Lego sets could be a very smart move. The WIRED Reviews team has a bunch of kids of all ages between us, and most of us are still big kids at heart, so we’ve tried a lot of board games and toys over the years.

The best Black Friday deals are well and truly on, and that includes some of the best family board games, best STEM toys, and best gifts for Lego lovers. I have handpicked a selection of WIRED-tested and approved options for you right here, so whether you’re buying gifts or just treating yourself, there’s sure to be something to put a smile on your face.

Updated November 28, 2027: We've added a few more deals on some of our favorite toys and games for kids.

Best Black Friday Toy Deals

What kid doesn’t love a marble run? This clever release from ThinkFun combines the fun of dropping marbles with logic puzzles that challenge kids to build a 3D maze that can guide the marble to the target end spot by building connected towers. It’s one of the best STEM toys we’ve tried, and it goes down a storm with most kids aged eight years and up.

This irresistible construction kit from our best STEM toys guide is a wonderful gift for kids of all ages. Clixo’s colorful, versatile magnetic pieces snap together, letting you build all kinds of three-dimensional shapes, from crowns to cats. The pieces stack neatly and are very compact when packed away. Clixo sets are also durable and washable, and you can play with them anywhere. Clixo kits are suitable for kids aged 4 and up.

The tough, translucent Magna-Tiles click together easily to form two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects. Kids love building houses, castles, vehicles, and whatever else they can imagine with these triangular and square magnetic tiles. The classic set is a great start, but be warned: There are themed sets, and you will end up buying more! I recommend the Undersea Adventure set.

One for older kids, the Camp Snap CS-8 is a (relatively) inexpensive video camera modeled on a 1960s home movie camera. Think of it as a digital Super 8 camera, a kind of antidote to the spec-chasing rat race of modern videography which also makes a great starter camera for children. It'll shoot 2.7K video, but that's not really the point, this is a camera that you pass around at parties, throw in your backpacks for day trips, and use without a second thought. —Scott Gilbertson

Sphero's Bolt coding robot is for any kid interested in programming. It's got a gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer, ambient light sensor, and the LED matrix for feedback. Kids can tap into all this through a visual programming interface, or older kids can dive into JavaScript or Python to control the Bolt. —Scott Gilbertson

This 175-piece kit takes you through the process of building a 4-cylinder engine. As someone who has built both this and rebuilt an actual engine (technically a 6-cylinder), this is very realistic, right down to all the tiny screws and springs you'll need to get it all together. And yes it “runs” or rather the pistons and valves move and will definitely give kids a very good working sense of how and internal combustion engine works. —Scott Gilbertson

Best Black Friday Board Game Deals

This Bluetooth-enabled chess board connects to an app on your phone, and you can play against remote players or yourself, or get AI coaching to improve your game. You can scale the assistance you want, with different-colored lights that advise you of moves as you pick up each piece. It’s perfect for beginners and kids. Particula also makes a Harry Potter-themed version that appears in our best smart chess boards guide.

Azul is about making mosaics by matching tiles with different patterns and colors to get the maximum possible score. It’s easy to grasp but supports many different tactical approaches and has surprising depth. The tiles and other components are high quality, and filling your board is deeply satisfying. Play moves quickly, and you can complete a game in less than an hour, but you will want to play again.

This beautifully themed game casts players as villains from the Star Wars universe, such as Darth Vader and Moff Gideon. If you’ve played other games in the Villainous series, you’ll know every character gets a unique set of victory conditions, and you can meddle with the other player’s attempts to win. There’s a definite learning curve, and some characters are easier to win with than others. This game is best for four players aged 10 years and up.

This immersive strategy game is all about gathering and trading resources to build roads, settlements, and cities on a randomly generated board of hexagonal tiles. Collecting enough points to win requires the right strategy and a bit of luck with dice rolls. My kids love the trading and the robber mechanic, which allows you to steal cards from your opponents and block their resources (though it can cause arguments). The game is perfect for three or four players and usually lasts around an hour.

The perfect spooky board game for classic horror fans, you must work cooperatively to defeat old horror-movie monsters like Dracula, the Wolf Man, and the Mummy. Cooperative games are perfect for family board game night, and this one is challenging enough that you really have to communicate well and work together if you want to avoid an untimely death and save the townsfolk.

Some of the best family board games are cooperative, so you can avoid those arguments that sometimes lead to board flipping and huffs, and Pandemic is a solid example. There’s a worldwide pandemic, and you must work together for the survival of mankind by jetting around the board and trying to halt the spread. Each player assumes a role, like a scientist or medic, with unique special powers, and you must strategize and coordinate to emerge alive.

Best Black Friday Lego Deals

This Lego set is perfect for a table or shelf once built; you can put the roses in a vase. You get a combination of 4 roses in full bloom, 4 blossoming roses, and 4 rosebuds, each with stems, along with 4 sprigs of white baby's breath flowers. There are three sets of instructions for building with family or friends, and this Lego set makes a great quirky gift. You can also get the Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees for $45 right now ($20 off).

More Lego sets on sale:

This fun parody throws the best of Batman’s movies into a blender with slapstick comedy and plenty of charm. You’ll scour Gotham for collectibles, uncover puzzles to solve, and face off against an army of thugs and villains. Melee combat is fun, as you counter and dodge to build combos, with a selection of classic gadgets at your disposal. This is the best Lego video game in recent years, and it’s perfect for split-screen couch co-op.

entries.title: Best Dyson Vacuum Black Friday Deals (2026): Up to $400 Off
entries.summary: If a Dyson vacuum is on yours (or a loved one’s) Christmas list, Black Friday is the best time to shop.
entries.content:
I’m often asked if Dyson products are really worth the money. As WIRED’s resident vacuum tester, I’ve tried every recent Dyson vacuum—from the newest, most powerful model to the long-favored V15 Detect—and I have a lot of thoughts on which ones you should buy and at what price. The best time to shop is during sale season, and lucky for you, Dyson Black Friday deals have arrived for you to scoop up a new stick vacuum or even a handy robot vacuum.

If a new vacuum is on your wishlist this holiday season, or a loved one's (my dad is obsessed with the Dyson), then Black Friday is your best shot at a great deal ahead of the holiday season. Here's the best sales happening on Dyson vacuums I've tested and love.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals; our team is actively hunting all weekend long. Want more robot vacuum options? Check out the Best Roborock Black Friday Deals.

Updated November 28, 2027: This story has been updated with more deals, and we checked that prices are still accurate.

  • Best Dyson Stick Vac Deal: Dyson V16 Piston Animal for $800 ($180 off)
  • Another Great Dyson Stick Vacuum Deal: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute for $600 ($290 off)
  • Best Dyson Wet Floor Cleaner Deal: Dyson Clean+Wash Hygiene Wet Cleaner for $400 ($100 off)
  • Best Dyson Robot Vac Deal: Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai for $800 ($400 off)

The Best Black Friday Dyson Stick Vacuum Deals

If you’re going to buy a Dyson vacuum on sale, you might as well go for one of the better ones. The V16 Piston Animal is Dyson’s most powerful stick vacuum, with 315 air-watts of power, some nice quality-of-life improvements in the body design, and an option to add the Submarine 2.0 mop head. I really liked this vacuum for the design upgrades and power level, but the price tag can be hard to stomach. It’s on sale fairly regularly, and there are a few different on-sale combos: The base vacuum is $180 off, bundling it with the Submarine head is $200 off, and the option with the charging Floor Dok is also $200 off. I love the Submarine head, but while I haven’t tested the vacuum with the Floor Dok yet, it’s the accessory I want most—having your cordless vacuum fully charged whenever you want it, and somewhere to store it, is really handy.

If you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also on sale. You can find it on sale on its own and bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit on Dyson's website, which gives it three extra attachments designed for cleaning your car. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, especially at this price.

Dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two. It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.

The PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact, and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.

The Best Black Friday Dyson Wet Floor Cleaner Deal

This wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal during Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1, with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.

The Best Black Friday Dyson Robot Vacuum Deal

The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m currently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.)

The Spot+Scrub Ai is much lower priced, and despite some dubious AI feature claims, it does a good job cleaning autonomously. It’s often discounted around this price, but the $400-off sale is a little better than what I saw during Prime Day.

More Black Friday Dyson Vacuum Deals

  • Dyson Car+Boat for $230 ($70 Off): You'll often find this handheld-only Dyson for this price, so it's not a deal you need to grab during Black Friday, but it's the preferred price to get it for if you want a Dyson-powered hand vac.
  • Dyson V8 Cyclone for $279 ($120 Off): Dyson revived the popular V8 stick vac earlier this year, but I didn't like it as much as I expected. Anyone going from the old V8 to this one will see a difference, and the Black Friday price is a better sale than we usually see for this vacuum.
  • Dyson Nurovi R1 for $400 ($150 Off): I haven't tested this newer robot vacuum from Dyson yet, but it's a cheaper vacuum-only design that was announced during IFA 2026. I wasn't blown away by the Nurovi R3, but if you wanted a current vacuum-only robot vacuum, this checks those boxes and is on sale.

entries.title: The Best Black Friday Sonos Deals (2026): Up to 34% Off
entries.summary: Always wanted a Sonos speaker but scared off by the price? Black Friday is one of the best times to shop the brand.
entries.content:
It's Black Friday weekend, and I am seeing some serious Black Friday Sonos deals this year. While there is nothing earth-shattering (don't expect to see any 50 percent offs here), I'm always on the lookout for a good Sonos deal, as the brand makes some of our favorite audio products. Black Friday deals like these below make all of their products easier to recommend (they tend to be a bit pricey, generally).

I've been reviewing audio products and covering major sale events like Black Friday for over four years. Below are the best Black Friday Sonos deals I found. I'll be sure to keep this updated through the weekend and Cyber Monday, though I don't expect much to change—brands like Sonos historically keep their discounts pretty consistent over the big shopping event.

Updated November 28: I added a note about the Sonos Ray and confirmed prices of all deals below.

Sonos Soundbars Deals

Sonos Subwoofers Deals

Sonos Home Speakers Deals

Sonos Portable Speakers Deals

I would argue that the Sonos Move 2 is more of a portable home Bluetooth speaker than a lightweight, compact, throw-it-in-your-bag for a trip to the beach-type speaker like the Roam 2 and Play above. Think of it like a portable, dust and water resistant version of the Era 100.

Sonos Headphones Deals

The new Sonos Ace Ultra headphones are not on sale, but the capable originals are. The Sonos Ace don't connect or sync to other Sonos products like the brand's speakers do, but they are capable stand-alone headphones, with clear sound, a comfortable fit, and a surprisingly good transparency mode.

Sonos Ray for $169 ($50 off): My issue with the Sonos Ray is that it doesn't connect over HDMI ARC, meaning, you cannot control it with your TV remote in many cases. That makes it a huge pain to use compared to any other Sonos soundbar. Go for the Beam (Gen 2) instead of this one.

entries.title: The 29 Very Best Amazon Black Friday Deals (2026): Up to 60% Off
entries.summary: For die-hard Amazon shoppers, the retailer’s “Black Friday Week” sale is still ongoing. Score discounts on our favorite (and tested) products through November 30.
entries.content:
Amazon’s Black Friday deals have been live since last week, giving shoppers a head start. But if you’ve been waiting until you’ve loaded up on turkey before loading up your cart, you’re still in luck: Amazon’s “Black Friday Week” sale runs until November 30 (Cyber Monday), giving you plenty of time to wrap up your shopping. To help you sift through the many products, we’ve highlighted some of our favorites below. If you’re a big Amazon shopper, now is a great time to fill those holiday wish lists and spend Black Friday with friends and family.

Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals, the Best Black Friday Deals Under $100, and the Best Black Friday TV Deals.

Updated November 27: We’ve checked sale pricing to ensure they’re still active.

Jump To

Best Amazon Black Friday Tech Deals

When Apple raised prices earlier this year, the once-affordable MacBook Air now starts at $1,300. Yet, the MacBook Air is still the best Apple laptop for most people, even some pro users, thanks to the M5 chipset’s power and efficiency. This Black Friday deal brings the 13-inch base model to around $1,000, close to its pre-increase price; we've seen it fluctuate between $989 and $1,049. Its 15-inch sibling is also on sale for $1,199, down from $1,499.

The Arc Ultra is a soundbar that does it right, delivering great all-around performance from a single speaker. Our current pick as the best soundbar you can buy, the Arc Ultra supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X surround sound to create cinema-quality audio in your living room. For a true surround setup, the Sonos Ultimate Immersive Set with Arc Ultra is also on sale and includes a subwoofer and two additional speakers.

The best iPad for most people isn’t one of Apple’s more powerful options, which says a lot. The base iPad runs on the older A16 chipset, but it can handle most of what people use a tablet for: streaming entertainment, web browsing, email, drawing, and even light productivity work. It’s great for casual users, including kids. This Black Friday deal brings the price closer to its previous MSRP, before Apple’s price increase. Check out more Black Friday iPad Deals.

While you can often find this router at this sale price, it’s still a deal for the best budget Wi-Fi router for a small home. It’s not the most powerful router, and it doesn’t support the 6 GHz band, but if your needs are basic, it will more than suffice.

With a WIRED rating of 9 out of 10, the XM6 is one of our favorite over-ear headphones, combining comfort with great sound quality and noise cancellation. This is the lowest price on Amazon; however, it has dropped to this price before. Note that Walmart and Best Buy are also offering the XM6 at this sale price.

Good gaming laptops are never cheap, and they’ve become even more expensive this year. If you need a recommendation that balances performance and budget, we recommend the Asus ROG Strix G16 with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060, one of our favorite budget gaming laptops. We prefer the RTX 5070 option, but it’s nearly $3,000. This on-sale model is more attainable.

The latest Echo Show 11 is our recommendation for the Best Alexa Smart Display. WIRED reviewer Nena Farrell found the screen bright and crisp, with immersive sound quality. Since the sale price matches the regular price of the smaller Echo Show 8, it’s a good deal—just $5 more than the sale price during Amazon’s October Prime Day event.

The Pixel 11-series phones from Google are among our favorite Android devices. Loaded with the latest software and Gemini AI features, the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL are our pick as the smartest Android smartphones. They’re also the only non-iPhones to support Qi2 wireless charging and magnetic mounting, so you can use MagSafe accessories. During Black Friday, you can get all for under $1,000 each—a terrific deal for a flagship phone—and they’re at their lowest price ever on Amazon.

High-quality three-in-one charging stands look terrific on a bedside table, but many cost over $100. This one from Mophie is one of our favorites, and it’s 49 percent off on Amazon right now.

The AirTag seems to be on sale all the time, but no matter—it’s currently the lowest price on Amazon and cheaper than buying from Apple. It’s one of the best Bluetooth trackers. If you can swing it, go for the four-pack.

Alongside the AirTag, the AirPods Max 2 and AirPods Pro 3 are also on sale. These are well-regarded among WIRED testers, but we recommend waiting until after Thanksgiving to see if they drop further—don’t worry, they are often on sale.

Phone accessories are aplenty on Amazon, but few look as good as Moft’s. You can pick up this ingenious wallet-kickstand hybrid that attaches to an iPhone via MagSafe, or peruse the rest of Moft’s Black Friday deals.

You can expect Amazon’s own devices to go on sale during Black Friday. While Blink’s security cameras didn’t make our short list, WIRED reviewer Simon Hill still thinks they’re worth considering, especially if you’re on a budget. A downer is that they only work with Alexa, but if that’s your smart home setup, it’s NBD. The latest version of its pan-tilt camera is usually $50, but it’s 60 percent off right now.

WIRED’s audio editor won’t stop praising Soundcore products, but he’s not wrong: This nascent brand (soon to be rebranded as Anker, its parent company) makes terrific audio products without the premium price. WIRED reviewer Louryn Strampe included this Bluetooth boom box in a roundup of her favorite festival gear. It’s the lowest price ever on Amazon currently, but it’s not the cheapest—keep an eye out at other retailers during Black Friday.

This EcoFlow portable battery is WIRED reviewer Simon Hill’s pick as the best power bank for laptops. It has a large 27,650-mAh capacity, which is plenty for charging smaller devices too. It’s great for travel since it’s allowed on a plane, and it has a retractable USB-C cable, so you can leave extras at home.

At $359, the second-gen Bose QuietComfort over-ear headphones seem overpriced considering the competition. But when they’re on sale at $199 to $219 (depending on the color), they suddenly become a great buy. As expected from Bose, the noise cancellation and sound quality are excellent. They are also comfortable, making them great travel companions. Note that the first-gen version is also on sale for around $169 (it’s frequently at this price), but it’s outdated, and we think you should spend $30 to $50 more on the latest version instead.

Amazon Black Friday Home and Kitchen Deals

Gone are the days of putting up holiday lights and then taking them down, only to do it again the next year. These outdoor lights are designed to stay up permanently; when they’re not displaying colorful holiday lights, they can shine white for regular everyday lighting. They work with any smart home platform, so you can control them via an app or a voice assistant.

WIRED Reviews Editor Kat Merck is our resident bird expert, having tested numerous bird feeders and doing extensive research on her feathered friends who visit her home. One of the best bird feeders she’s used is on sale at Amazon at the lowest price ever. The Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 is easy to clean and has a solar roof for wire-free camera charging. The app even has a handy bird-identification feature to help you determine what species stopped by.

The Vitamix 5200 isn't cheap, even on sale for Black Friday, but it is unquestionably the best blender you can buy. It will very likely last a lifetime—I've had mine for almost ten years now and it doesn't have a scratch on it and functions just like it did the day I bought it. Which, for the record, was during a Black Friday sale. —Scott Gilbertson

KitchenAid's stand mixers are justifiably legendary. Look at it, it's the stand mixer. The 5-quart stainless steel bowl is big enough for nearly any recipe, and the tilt-back head makes removing it a cinch. The more expensive Professional model is better for thick doughs and larger recipes (it has a more powerful motor), but for most of us the Artisan will do the job.

Breville primarily competes with itself when it comes to toaster ovens: The Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro, alongside the Joule version with upgraded software, is almost certainly the best of its kind. It has incredible precision, it toasts evenly across the oven, and it can air-fry nuggets to perfect crispness, dehydrate fruit, and also roast an entire sweet potato. This is the cheapest we'll see it until the holidays, and for a little more than $300, it cooks and air-fries everything to perfection.

It seems like every appliance maker offers an air fryer, but if you want the best, the Typhur Dome 2 should be at the top of your shortlist. It’s also on sale this Black Friday, which makes this “splurge” item a bit easier on the holiday budget. Our reviewer found it works fast during testing, and it can bake as well as cook a pizza or steak.

As a premium home appliance maker, Dyson doesn’t make cheap products. Which is why Black Friday is a good time to see what might go on sale. Right now, our top pick for the most affordable Dyson vacuum cleaner is even cheaper—the lowest price we’ve seen yet. It works on both hard and carpeted floors, and its brush system can handle all sorts of debris.

Love them or hate them, but pod-based coffee makers are popular for their convenience. The Nespresso Vertuo Pop+ is our recommended espresso pod maker, and the Deluxe model is under $100. It has a larger water tank than the standard version, and the Vertuo pods are recyclable. For more savings on coffee-related products, check out our Early Black Friday Espresso Machine Deals.

WIRED’s home-cleaning expert, Nena Farrell, recommended only three robot vacuums, naming this Eufy floor-sweeping automaton her budget pick. It’s 53 percent off right now—the lowest price ever on Amazon—for a robovac with great suction power and a self-cleaning roller mop.

With quality espresso machines costing $500 and more (way, way more), a budget option seems improbable. Yet, this De’Longhi fits the bill. entries.title: 7 Pro Tips to Get More Out of the Google Health App
entries.summary: Google has replaced the fitness tracking software for your Fitbit or Wear OS watch with an app called Google Health. Here’s how to make it do more than just the basics.
entries.content:
If you've been using the Fitbit app in recent years, you'll know that it's now been replaced by Google Health. (Google bought Fitbit back in 2019.) The app will eventually replace Google Fit too, though we don't know exactly when that will be. Google has previously said it will happen before the end of the year.

While many features have been carried over into Google Health from its predecessors, some haven't. There have also been new additions, and a lot of rearranging has gone on too, so it can take a while to figure out exactly where everything is.

Whether you're a veteran from the Google Fit or Fitbit days, or you've just installed Google Health for the first time to use with a new device, these tips will help you explore everything the app has to offer and get the most out of it.

1. You Don’t Need a Wearable

If you've been waiting to buy a device to track your steps before installing Google Health, you don't have to. You can still get the step-tracking features from the app, as long as you carry your phone with you on all your walks and runs.

Tap the Connections icon (top left), then Phone to start pulling in data from your Android or iOS smartphone. If you later add a wearable, you can switch to this for steps—or keep them both enabled (handy if you forget your tracker at home one day, for example).

2. Organize Your Today Page

The Today page is the first one you see when you open the Google Health app, so it makes sense to fill it with the stats that actually matter to you, rather than the metrics the app picks. Tap the pen icon just underneath the top bank of widgets to make changes.

You're able to switch between Standard view and Expanded view, depending on how much health and fitness information you want to see at once. In both views, you can swipe right or left to see more widgets.

Tap the + (plus) icon next to any widget you want to add to the Today page, and the - (minus) icon next to any widget you want to remove. Hiding widgets doesn't do anything to your fitness data, it just means that data isn't shown on the Today view.

3. Add Workouts Manually

You don't have to rely on your fitness tracker, smartwatch, or phone to capture all of your movement. To add something manually, tap Log on the Today view, then Activity, and pick the activity type—like Walk, Basketball, Indoor climbing, or whatever it is.

The app asks you to fill out key details, like the start and end points of the activity, before saving the record. You can manually add lots of other information from the same screens, from the hours you’ve slept to the meals you've had.

4. Set Your Goals

There are various parts of the Google Health interface, including the widgets on the Today page, where you'll see references to your health and fitness goals. These aren't going to be all that useful to you if you just leave the default values in place.

To make these metrics more meaningful, tap your profile picture (top right), then choose Google Health settings > Activity. You'll find numerous goals listed here, together with a few other settings, like whether or not to detect activities automatically.

Tap on any goal to set it or edit it. These targets affect the layout of screens throughout the app, and you might get notifications about them too, from time to time—if you don't want this, choose Manage notifications from the Activity screen.

5. Ensure Fitness Tracking Accuracy

You'll of course want your fitness tracker or smartwatch to be logging everything as accurately as possible. Even if the step counts are only off by a little each day, that can add up to a big difference over the weeks and months.

There are two settings to check here: If you tap your profile picture (top right), then choose Google Health settings > Activity, you can set your Stride length. This lets you give Google Health more precise measurements for your gait, whether walking or running.

Second, tap the Connections icon (top left), then your wearable. Choose Device preferences, and you can tell the app which wrist your wearable is usually on, which should mean more accurate step and movement tracking.

6. Upgrade for More Features

You may have seen mentions of Google Health Premium in the app or seen pop-ups about it, but what exactly is it? And what do you get for your money? The subscription replaces the old Fitbit Premium and works along similar lines.

For $10 a month, you get personalized and adaptable health plans that give you specific instructions for reaching your health and fitness goals. You also get a Gemini-powered AI Coach that gives you workout recaps and fitness advice based on the metrics you're recording.

The sleep summaries are more detailed in terms of sleep stages and the sleep scoring system. You also get access to a library of guided workouts and mindfulness sessions in the app.

One extra note: If you're signed up for one of Google's AI plans at the $20-per-month tier or higher, you get Google Health Premium thrown in as part of it (as well as Google Home Premium and YouTube Premium Lite).

7. Turn the AI Coach Off (or On)

It's possible that you want all the Google Health Premium extras but find the AI Coach a bit intrusive. It does take a very proactive stance when it comes to giving you tips and pointers, but it can be a bit too eager to help.

To hide it from view, tap your profile picture (top right), then Google Health settings > Coach. From here you can opt out of the Coach feature entirely or just hide the main insights from view. (You'll still be able to ask questions about your data.) When you need the coach’s encouragement and you want to turn it back on, you can do so in the same place.

entries.title: Swift Saw the Secrets of Space Before Falling to Earth
entries.summary: Designed for a two-year mission, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory saw thousands of gamma-ray bursts and stars being torn apart by black holes over 22 years before burning up in Earth’s atmosphere.
entries.content:
NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has concluded its scientific mission, which spanned just under 22 years. As its orbital altitude fell below 275 kilometers (171 miles), it could no longer continue stable astronomical observations, and it reentered the atmosphere on November 4 over North Sumatra, Indonesia.

Swift had been launched on November 20, 2004, as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer, and it began operations the following month. In addition to a gamma-ray-burst alert telescope, it was equipped with ultraviolet and visible-light telescopes as well as an x-ray telescope, and was designed as a multi-wavelength observation satellite capable of rapidly pinpointing the locations of gamma-ray bursts—the most powerful explosions in the universe. In 2018, following the death of its first principal investigator, Neil Gehrels, NASA renamed the mission in his honor.

Tracking Gamma-Ray Bursts

The development of the Swift space telescope was driven by the difficulty of tracking gamma-ray bursts. “Swift was designed as a satellite dedicated to studying gamma-ray bursts, outbursts that came and went so quickly that no one could target them with large telescopes to learn more,” explains S. Bradley Cenko, the mission’s principal investigator at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.

Swift detected a gamma-ray burst, pinpointed its location, relayed the information to other observatories, and then swiveled its telescope to capture images before the afterglow faded; this sequence of operations was usually finished in about a minute. Speed was particularly critical for short gamma-ray bursts, in which the emissions end in less than two seconds. Before Swift was launched, it was not possible to pinpoint the location quickly and accurately enough to observe the afterglow.

In May 2005, Swift quickly turned toward the gamma-ray burst GRB 050509B, which lasted only 0.03 second, and detected 11 x-ray photons. This was the first short gamma-ray burst for which an afterglow was detected. This observation corroborated long-standing theoretical models suggesting that short bursts are most likely caused by the merger of two neutron stars, celestial bodies with a mass comparable to the sun compressed to the size of a city.

Its flexible observation planning system is another reason why Swift was regarded as a versatile tool for astronomy. This is because astronomers could request target-of-opportunity observations, which allowed commands to be sent from the ground in as little as a few minutes.

It also allowed for the setup of monitoring programs to observe specific celestial objects for periods ranging from minutes to months, and it was possible to schedule observations of up to 75 distinct celestial objects per day. Furthermore, it played a role in sending alerts to other space- and ground-based facilities to coordinate additional observations.

Swift observed more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and more than 1,400 supernova explosions. It also witnessed stars being torn apart by black holes, monitored active galaxies, and conducted all-sky x-ray surveys; the data from these observations contributed to approximately 7,000 scientific papers. The entire dataset—including approximately 22 years’ worth of brightness measurements and more than 1.5 million images from ultraviolet and visible-light telescopes—is publicly available and amounts to about 12 terabytes.

Rescue Mission Attempted but Abandoned

The Swift observatory was circling in low Earth orbit. At this altitude even the outermost layer of the atmosphere creates air resistance on satellites. However, Swift lacked thrusters to maintain its orbit, and its altitude continued to drop.

As a result, its altitude—which was approximately 585 kilometers (364 miles) at launch—had dropped to about 363 kilometers as of June 18, 2026. In recent years, increased solar activity has caused Earth’s atmosphere to expand, causing the telescope to descend faster than initially predicted.

NASA engineers had long predicted that Swift’s altitude would drop to approximately 300 kilometers by the fall of 2026, at which point a recovery spacecraft would no longer be able to approach it safely. Consequently, NASA decided not to issue a standard request for proposals and instead asked three companies with which it had already signed technology development contracts to explore the feasibility of providing orbital services. In September 2025, NASA signed a $30 million contract with the space startup Katalyst Space Technologies.

The original plan was for the small satellite LINK to capture and dock with Swift using three robotic arms, raise its orbit to a safe operational altitude, and resume scientific observations. Since there was only one year to complete this task, Katalyst manufactured components in-house when suppliers could not meet their deadlines and streamlined testing procedures. LINK was launched on July 3, 2026, aboard a Northrop Grumman Pegasus XL rocket.

However, during in-orbit testing, a malfunction occurred in LINK’s attitude-control system, and it was determined that capturing Swift and raising its orbit would be difficult. In response, NASA and Katalyst announced on August 19 that the operation would be canceled, and the mission was redefined as an in-orbit demonstration.

LINK raised its orbit to align with Swift, deployed its three robotic arms, and simultaneously fired its three ion thrusters, successfully approaching the telescope to a distance of 12 to 15 kilometers (7 to 9 miles). Nevertheless, NASA announced that LINK would not approach Swift any closer during the remainder of its operational life in orbit. LINK subsequently reentered Earth’s atmosphere on September 25.

Following the decision to abandon the orbital raise, the Swift operations team announced a plan to continue observations for as long as possible in the time left. On August 26, they restarted the ultraviolet- and visible-light telescopes and the x-ray telescope—which had been shut down in preparation for the rescue mission—and successfully captured images of Tycho’s supernova remnant, located approximately 13,000 light-years away. But as the altitude dropped below 275 kilometers, the telescope was no longer able to maintain a stable lock on its target, and the scientific mission concluded with the final observation on October 20.

“Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long,” said Sean Domagall-Goldman, director of the Astrophysics Division at NASA headquarters. To ensure it can continue to respond swiftly to cosmic phenomena even after Swift is gone, NASA is considering ways to utilize and expand its existing fleet of space telescopes.

This story was originally published in WIRED Japan and has been translated from Japanese.

entries.title: Best Black Friday Robot Vacuum Deals from Roborock (2026): Up to 60% Off
entries.summary: A few of the best robot vacuums I’ve tested from the brand are at their lowest prices ever.
entries.content:
Robot vacuums are more expensive than ever, with models from popular brands starting anywhere from $1,200 to $2,000. But you don't have to pay such a high price tag for a great model—you just have to wait for a good sale, and Black Friday deals are the best one's you'll find all year. I'm particularly impressed by Roborock's robot vacuum deals. The brand has a huge range of robot vacuums that we love, with great navigation and varying levels of mopping, suction power, and bonus features, depending on how much you want to spend. With some models up to 63 percent off, this is the best time to shop.

Updated November 28, 2026: I added new Roborock deals to the list and made sure all prices were up to date.

  • Roborock's Best Budget Vac at its Best Price: Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro for $450 ($350 off)
  • A Powerful, But Still Affordable Roller-Mop Vac: Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow for $550 ($450 off)
  • If You Want Super Powerful Suction, Plus a Roller Mop: Roborock Saros 20 Flow for $1,300 ($400 off)
  • If You Want Roborock's Arm Attachment: Roborock Saros Z70 with OmniGrip for $950 ($700 off)

The Best Black Friday Vacuum Deals from Roborock

The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro launched in late summer as the newest addition to the brand's more affordable Qrevo line, and it quickly landed as a pick on my guide to the Best Robot Vacuums. It's often on sale for around $600, and thanks to Black Friday, it's down to the lowest price I've seen it for: $450, nearly half off.

Overall, Roborock's vacuums are great, but I've been especially impressed by this one's corner cleaning, thanks to its extendable mop arm. It won't always spot cords, but it does a better job at navigating furniture and getting underneath my cabinets than more expensive robot vacuums I've tested.

If you'd rather have a roller-mop-style robot vacuum, the Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is another great option from Roborock's Qrevo line. This one came out in January of this year, and our reviewer instantly loved it.

The Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is a more expensive robot vacuum than the Qrevo 2 since it comes with the brand's SpriaFlow roller-mop. The internal roller spans nearly the entire width of the vacuum and can extend to edge-clean your home. It even has a built-in scraper to move dirty water into the tank instead of rolling it back onto the floor. If you're looking for an affordable mopping powerhouse, this is the one to choose. It's also nearly half off, down to $550 off the $1,000 price tag.

There's the affordable Qrevo line from Roborock, and then there's the higher-end Saros line. While neither I nor former WIRED reviewer Adrienne So were particularly impressed with the Saros 20, I've been much happier with the performance of the Saros 20 Flow. Like the Curv 2 Flow, it has a roller mop instead of spinning mop pads, and it did well in my mopping tests. It also didn't leave debris around, even with its high suction of 36,000 Pa.

It's one of Roborock's most expensive vacuums, and it comes across while using it—it feels very premium. I've been preferring it over the new Dyson robot vacuum I've been testing. Luckily, you can get it on sale right now for Black Friday. It still isn't cheap at $1,300, but it's one of my all-time favorites and one I have kept coming back to after trying other models.

If you're looking for something truly unique in a robot vacuum, Roborock's Saros Z70 might be what you're looking for. It has a mechanical arm built into it to pick up small items like socks while it vacuums, which sounds handy, but it didn't work as well as we'd hoped during testing. Still, maybe you feel that's the solution you've been dying for. If that's the case, it's available for a nice discount right now at $950.

It also packs 22,000 Pa of suction (not as powerful as the Saros 20 Flow, but still plenty of suction to clean carpets and rugs alike!) and still executes fast, effective cleaning. But the battery life on this vacuum isn't as long as that of other Roborocks we've tested. Again, you're mostly getting this one for the mechanical arm.

  • Roborock Q7 M5+ for $200 ($230 off): One of the brand's more basic options, but still fit with vacuuming, mopping, and an auto-empty dock.
  • Roborock Q10 S5+ for $320 ($180 off): If you're willing to spend $30 more, this Q10 has better mopping and a larger battery than the Q7 above.
  • Roborock Qrevo S Pro for $380 ($320 off): The Qrevo 2 Pro has better brushes and corner performance, but this S Pro is no slouch either, and is a bit cheaper right now.
